test_title: PYST 8: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct direct sentence of the following sentence.

He said that the lights had gone off during the storm.

options.text: He said, "The lights go off during the storm."
He said, "The lights had gone off during the storm."
He said, "The lights went off during the storm."
He said, "The lights have gone off during the storm."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** Direct speech involves quoting the exact words spoken by a person, enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Verb Tense:** The indirect speech "had gone off" remains the same in direct speech as "had gone off" because the tense is already in the past perfect.
 
• **Quotation Marks:** Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks to indicate the exact words spoken.
 
• **Reporting Verb:** In the given sentence, "He said" is the reporting verb and is retained without any changes.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech starts with a capital letter inside the quotation marks.
 
• The sentence ends with a full stop inside the quotation marks.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said, 'The lights had gone off during the storm.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "He said, 'The lights go off during the storm.'"
 
 
• Incorrect because the present simple tense "go off" changes the meaning and does not match the past perfect tense in the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He said, 'The lights went off during the storm.'"
 
 
• Incorrect because the past simple tense "went off" alters the original meaning conveyed by the past perfect tense "had gone off."
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said, 'The lights have gone off during the storm.'"
 
 
• Incorrect because the present perfect tense "have gone off" is inconsistent with the past perfect tense in the original sentence.
 
 
</ul
